candidates.title: Directed codebook repulsion with control-geometry anchoring
candidates.falsifier: Reject at the probe if the loss is unchanged when source and target are exchanged, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite, or codebook updates reduce level-0 usage balance, L1-to-L2 branches per code, train-to-test frequency stability, or sequence information relative to control. The cold-run falsifier is no increase in pair-level ER or no Stage-3 recall@10 improvement over 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: The soft mixtures may be too diffuse or poorly aligned with hard assignments, so the term can move codebook vectors without producing useful hard-SID changes. If the repulsive updates distort Voronoi regions, they may reduce prefix branching, sequence information, or held-out frequency stability even while pairwise ER rises.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The hinge differentiates through both soft assignments and their weighted codebook sums. Its directed displacement pushes the source- and target-associated soft codeword mixtures apart along the observed source-to-target direction when their projected separation is below the margin. It does not minimize pair-codeword distance or pull endpoint codewords together; the force is repulsive along the pair direction. The proposed margin and weight are finite, and assignment churn plus pairwise codeword separation must be checked at the probe.

candidates.title: Directed soft-assignment separation with branch-preserving occupancy constraint
candidates.falsifier: Reject at the probe if source-target exchange leaves the loss unchanged, declared gradients are zero or non-finite, or exported-code diagnostics show lower sequence information, fewer L1-to-L2 branches per code, greater level-0 usage concentration, or greater train-to-test frequency drift than control. The cold-run falsifier is no Stage-3 recall@10 gain over 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: The minibatch occupancy floor may be noisy or conflict with the learned marginal frequencies, creating broad soft assignments that do not translate to better hard-code branching. The ordered KL could also improve pairwise separation while losing sequence information or increasing train-to-test frequency drift.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The ordered KL differentiates through source and target distances to codebook vectors and seeks distinct, predictive endpoint distributions; the occupancy floor pushes underused codewords to receive soft mass in each endpoint role. Neither term attracts the two endpoint codewords: the KL compares distributions in an ordered direction, and the floor acts on marginal endpoint-role usage rather than pairwise codeword distances. This is not a guarantee that hard assignments retain branches, so the probe must measure hard level-0 concentration and L1-to-L2 branching.

candidates.title: Behaviour-residual directional transport with codebook covariance whitening
candidates.falsifier: Reject at the probe if exchanging source and target does not change the loss, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite, or the resulting code diagnostics violate any requirement: level-0 usage more concentrated than control, fewer L1-to-L2 branches per code, greater train-to-test frequency drift, or lower sequence information. The cold-run falsifier is no improvement in Stage-3 recall@10 over 0.06406796775709883.
candidates.risk: Residual covariance can be ill-conditioned or dominated by common transitions, making whitening amplify noisy directions despite stabilization. The fixed codebook-radius target may also oppose a useful learned scale. The resulting hard codes could lose sequence information or worsen frequency drift even if residual-direction projection improves.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The hinge differentiates through the soft endpoint assignments and codeword projections, pushing the target-role soft code projection ahead of the source-role projection along the covariance-whitened behaviour residual. The radius term acts on each codeword relative to the codebook mean, not on endpoint pairs, and discourages codebook-wide radial contraction or expansion. There is no pairwise attraction term; the directed residual projection is a separation signal. The covariance is detached to keep the gradient finite and avoid higher-order batch interactions.
